_comment: SENTINEL (index >= 90, excluded from the coverage metric by design): this is an ENVIRONMENT probe, not a pitfall fixture -- it reads the install feature flags out of deal.II's config.h and reports which of the catalog's assumed features (MPI, p4est, PETSc, Trilinos, SLEPc) this build actually has. It was previously keyed adaptive_refinement::0, a physics that does not exist in the deal.II registry, so it credited no claim while looking like coverage; rekeyed to the sentinel range on 2026-08-06 so that it plainly credits none. THE CLAIM IT WAS CITED FOR IS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED HERE (2026-08-08, measured). It was 'the evidence behind the parallel_poisson cannot be verified on this host finding: MPI, P4EST, PETSC, TRILINOS and SLEPC are all undefined in this install'. Executed: the install this probe reads, /usr/include/deal.II 9.1.1 -- which is also the header tree the deal.II fixtures compile against -- reports features_on=['DEAL_II_WITH_HDF5', 'DEAL_II_WITH_LAPACK', 'DEAL_II_WITH_MPI', 'DEAL_II_WITH_MUPARSER', 'DEAL_II_WITH_P4EST', 'DEAL_II_WITH_PETSC', 'DEAL_II_WITH_SLEPC', 'DEAL_II_WITH_TRILINOS'] and features_off=['DEAL_II_WITH_METIS'], with catalog_claims_install_doesnt_support=[]. All five are ON. The build with them undefined is the OTHER one on this host, ~/dealii/build 9.8.0-pre, which is exactly what T2_MUTATE=1 points at. So the finding rested on a measurement of a different install than the one in use, and the fixture could not tell the two apart because all five of its expectations were bare `key=` prefixes. Tier-2 for dealii adaptive_refinement#: probe install feature flags from config.h to expose the gap between catalog claims (p4est, MPI, PETSc, Trilinos, SLEPc) and what the current conda-forge dealii-9.1.1 install actually has compiled. The 9.1.1 default has all parallelism features UNDEFINED — a serial-only build. This fixture PASSES whenever it can detect ANY dealii install and produce a feature report; it fails only when config.h is missing entirely. Output 'catalog_claims_install_doesnt_support' is the falsification ledger for the current install state — when task #30 (deal.II rebuild) lands, the same fixture will record an empty ledger. Verified empirically 2026-06-01. MUTATION CONTROL (2026-08-07): MUTATION APPLIED AND IT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE — the hook is left in source.py, no recipe is declared, because a declared recipe that survives reads as a defect rather than as the finding. T2_MUTATE=1 points the same probe at the OTHER deal.II on this host, whose flags are the mirror image of the one normally found, and the fixture STILL PASSES. Measured 2026-08-07: unmutated it read /usr/include/deal.II/base/config.h (dealii_version=9.1.1) and reported features_on=[HDF5, LAPACK, MPI, MUPARSER, P4EST, PETSC, SLEPC, TRILINOS], features_off=[METIS], catalog_claims_install_doesnt_support=[]; mutated it read ~/dealii/build/include/deal.II/base/config.h (dealii_version=9.8.0) and reported features_off=[HDF5, MPI, P4EST, PETSC, SLEPC, TRILINOS] and FIVE broken catalog claims. Same fixture, opposite report, both green. That is structural: every expect_in_output string is a bare `key=` prefix that main() prints unconditionally, so the only thing this fixture asserts is that SOME config.h was found — never what it says. Two consequences worth reading twice. First, the sentence above, 'MPI, P4EST, PETSC, TRILINOS and SLEPC are all undefined in this install', is FALSE for the install this fixture actually reads on this host, and the fixture passes anyway. Second, an expectation naming a measured value (e.g. a specific features_off entry) would make it discriminate; that change is deliberately NOT made here, because tuning a fixture until its mutation goes red is how a control stops being evidence. Re-run by hand: `cd <fixture dir> && T2_MUTATE=1 ~/Schreibtisch/open-fem-agent/.venv/bin/python source.py`. FIXED 2026-08-08 (expectations changed): the probe now prints one feature[<FLAG>]=on|off line per flag and the fixture pins them, plus dealii_version and an empty catalog ledger. Measured: unmutated reads /usr/include/deal.II/base/config.h, dealii_version=9.1.1, the five parallel flags on, METIS off, ledger []; T2_MUTATE=1 reads ~/dealii/build/include/deal.II/base/config.h, dealii_version=9.8.0, the five parallel flags OFF, METIS ON and a five-entry ledger -- so every pinned expectation flips and the fixture goes red where it used to pass against either install. The mutation hook is no longer a recorded non-discriminating control; it is the control.
